children: Gold loans have surged more than fourfold in two years, helped by rising gold prices and a relaxation in Reserve Bank of India norms that allows borrowers to raise a larger loan against their jewellery, particularly for smaller-ticket borrowing.

Loans against gold jewellery rose 4.4 times to Rs 5.52 lakh crore in July 2026 from Rs 1.24 lakh crore in July 2024, according to RBI data collated by Moneycontrol. The outstanding amount stood at Rs 2.06 lakh crore in July 2025.
The sharp increase has also changed the composition of personal lending.
Gold loans accounted for just 2.2 percent of total personal loans in July 2024. Their share more than doubled to 4.8 percent in July 2025 before climbing further to 7.7 percent in July 2026.
In contrast, the combined share of education, consumer durable and credit-card loans declined from 7.7 percent in July 2024 to 7.4 percent a year later and further to 6.7 percent in July 2026.
South India remains the gold-loan heartland
Despite the rapid expansion across the country, gold-backed borrowing remains heavily concentrated in southern India.

The five southern states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana and Kerala together accounted for more than 70 percent of the outstanding gold-loan portfolio as of June 2026, according to CRIF High Mark's How India Lendsreport.
Tamil Nadu alone accounted for 30 percent of the portfolio, followed by Andhra Pradesh at 15.9 percent and Karnataka at 10.2 percent.
But the geography of growth is becoming more dispersed.

Uttar Pradesh's gold-loan portfolio expanded 122.8 percent year-on-year as of June, the fastest among the 10 largest states tracked by CRIF. West Bengal recorded growth of 99.7 percent, Rajasthan 91.2 percent, while Gujarat and Telangana expanded 80.5 percent each.
RBI norms provide a boost
Apart from the increase in gold prices, regulatory changes have made smaller gold loans more attractive for borrowers.
The RBI’s new gold and silver collateral framework introduced a tiered loan-to-value, or LTV, structure for consumption loans.

Under the revised rules, lenders can provide loans of up to 85 percent of the value of pledged gold for total borrowing of up to Rs 2.5 lakh. The ceiling is 80 percent for loans above Rs 2.5 lakh and up to Rs 5 lakh, while loans above Rs 5 lakh remain capped at 75 percent.
PNB sees good growth
Banks have also stepped up their focus on the segment.

Asked in an August interview about the sharp expansion in Punjab National Bank's gold-loan portfolio, PNB MD and CEO Ashok Chandra said the bank had previously been a relatively small player in the business.
But clearer RBI guidelines have encouraged the bank to push the product more actively.
“Bank has started putting forward for the gold loan also. We are seeing good growth happening in the gold loan sector,” Chandra said.
The other major driver has been the rise in the value of the collateral itself.
Gold futures for October delivery on the Multi Commodity Exchange were trading at Rs 1,52,511 per 10 grams on September 22.
Secured lending gains favour
The shift has also come as lenders have become more cautious about parts of the unsecured retail market.
Unlike credit-card loans and most consumer lending, gold loans are backed by an asset that lenders can liquidate in the event of default.

Asset quality in the segment remains relatively comfortable. CRIF data show that loans overdue by 31-90 days accounted for 0.9 percent of the gold-loan portfolio in June, while another 0.3 percent was in the 91-180 day bucket and 0.2 percent was overdue by more than 180 days.

title: Gold loans surge 4.4x, gain share in personal credit amid slower unsecured growth
